## Assignment 5 - Load data into Spark, Create Tables and Queries
```{python}


from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import ArrayType
import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
import plotly.io as pio
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)
pio.renderers.default = "notebook+notebook_connected+vscode"

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("CareerCompassData").getOrCreate()

from pathlib import Path

data_dir = Path("./Jobs_2026")  
parquet_files = sorted(data_dir.glob("*.parquet"))

df = spark.read.parquet(*[str(path) for path in parquet_files])

model_source_cols = [
    "SALARY_TO", "SALARY_FROM", "SALARY",
    "MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE", "MAX_YEARS_EXPERIENCE", "DURATION",
    "EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME", "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME", "REMOTE_TYPE_NAME",
    "IS_INTERNSHIP", "COMPANY_IS_STAFFING"
]
df = df.select(*model_source_cols)

# Cast numeric columns to double and replace NaN with null
numeric_cols = ["SALARY_TO", "SALARY_FROM", "SALARY",
                "MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE", "MAX_YEARS_EXPERIENCE", "DURATION"]

for c in numeric_cols:
    df = df.withColumn(c, F.expr("try_cast(`" + c + "` as double)"))
    df = df.withColumn(
        c,
        F.when(F.col(c).isNull() | F.isnan(F.col(c)), None).otherwise(F.col(c))
    )

# REMOTE_TYPE_NAME and EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME — ArrayType: explode directly
for col_name in ["REMOTE_TYPE_NAME", "EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME"]:
    if isinstance(df.schema[col_name].dataType, ArrayType):
        df = df.withColumn(col_name, F.explode_outer(F.col(col_name)))

# Normalize REMOTE_TYPE_NAME
df = df.withColumn(
    "REMOTE_TYPE_NAME",
    F.when(F.col("REMOTE_TYPE_NAME") == "On-site", "Onsite")
     .when(F.col("REMOTE_TYPE_NAME").isNull() | (F.col("REMOTE_TYPE_NAME") == "Unknown"), "Unknown")
     .otherwise(F.col("REMOTE_TYPE_NAME"))
)

# EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME — comma-separated string: split then explode
df = df.withColumn(
    "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME",
    F.explode_outer(F.split(F.col("EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME"), r",\s*"))
)
df = df.withColumn("EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME", F.trim(F.col("EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME")))

# Normalize EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME — collapse all variations to canonical labels
e = F.lower(F.col("EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME"))
df = df.withColumn(
    "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME",
    F.when(e.contains("intern"),                           "Internship")
     .when(e.contains("per diem") | e.contains("perdiem"), "Per Diem")
     .when(e.contains("temp"),                             "Temporary")
     .when(e.contains("contract"),                         "Contract")
     .when(e.contains("part"),                             "Part Time")
     .when(e.contains("permanent"),                        "Permanent")
     .when(e.contains("remote"),                           "Remote")
     .when(e.contains("full"),                             "Full Time")
     .otherwise(None)
)

# Replace empty strings with null across all string columns
for col_name in ["REMOTE_TYPE_NAME", "EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME", "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME"]:
    df = df.withColumn(
        col_name,
        F.when(F.trim(F.col(col_name)) == "", None).otherwise(F.col(col_name))
    )

print("---Diagnostic check, No need to print it in the final doc---")
df.printSchema()
df.show(5)

df.groupBy("EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
df.groupBy("EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()
df.groupBy("REMOTE_TYPE_NAME").count().orderBy("count", ascending=False).show()


```

###  Feature Engineering 
```{python}
from pyspark.ml import Pipeline
from pyspark.ml.feature import StringIndexer, OneHotEncoder, VectorAssembler
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# ── Feature selection ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
continuous_cols = [
    "SALARY_FROM",
    "MAX_YEARS_EXPERIENCE",
    "DURATION",
    "MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE",
]
categorical_cols = [
    "REMOTE_TYPE_NAME",
    "EMPLOYMENT_TYPE_NAME",
    "EDUCATION_LEVELS_NAME",
]
target_col = "SALARY_FROM"   # ← use SALARY_FROM (cleaner numeric) as target

# ── 1. Cast all continuous cols to double (tolerate bad strings) ──────────────
df_clean = df
for c in continuous_cols:
    df_clean = df_clean.withColumn(c, F.expr(f"try_cast(`{c}` as double)"))

# ── 2. Replace empty strings in categoricals ──────────────────────────────────
for c in categorical_cols:
    df_clean = df_clean.withColumn(
        c, F.when(F.trim(F.col(c)) == "", None).otherwise(F.col(c))
    )

# ── 3. Only require target + MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE to be non-null ──────────────
df_clean = df_clean.dropna(subset=[target_col, "MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE"])

print(f"Rows in raw data     : {df.count():,}")
print(f"Rows after cleaning  : {df_clean.count():,}")

# ── StringIndexer + OneHotEncoder ─────────────────────────────────────────────
indexers = [
    StringIndexer(inputCol=c, outputCol=f"{c}_idx", handleInvalid="keep")
    for c in categorical_cols
]
encoders = [
    OneHotEncoder(inputCol=f"{c}_idx", outputCol=f"{c}_ohe")
    for c in categorical_cols
]
ohe_cols = [f"{c}_ohe" for c in categorical_cols]

# ── VectorAssembler (handleInvalid="keep" fills missing features with 0) ──────
assembler = VectorAssembler(
    inputCols=continuous_cols + ohe_cols,
    outputCol="features",
    handleInvalid="keep"
)

# ── Pipeline ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
pipeline_model = Pipeline(stages=indexers + encoders + [assembler]).fit(df_clean)
df_featured = pipeline_model.transform(df_clean)

# ── Polynomial feature: MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE² ─────────────────────────────────
df_featured = df_featured.withColumn(
    "MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE_SQ",
    F.pow(F.col("MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE"), 2)
)

# ── Assemble polynomial features ──────────────────────────────────────────────
poly_assembler = VectorAssembler(
    inputCols=continuous_cols + ["MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE_SQ"] + ohe_cols,
    outputCol="features_poly",
    handleInvalid="keep"
)
df_poly = poly_assembler.transform(df_featured)

# ── Train/test split ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
train_df, test_df = df_poly.randomSplit([0.8, 0.2], seed=42)
print(f"Training rows : {train_df.count():,}")
print(f"Testing  rows : {test_df.count():,}")

# ── Show final structure ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
show_cols = [target_col] + continuous_cols + categorical_cols + \
            ["MIN_YEARS_EXPERIENCE_SQ", "features", "features_poly"]

df_poly.select(*show_cols).printSchema()
df_poly.select(*show_cols).show(5, truncate=True)
```

###  Linear Regression 
```{python}
from pyspark.ml.regression import LinearRegression
from pyspark.ml.evaluation import RegressionEvaluator
from pyspark.sql.functions import udf, col, isnan
from pyspark.sql.types import BooleanType
from scipy import stats
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import math

boolean_cols = ["IS_INTERNSHIP", "COMPANY_IS_STAFFING"]

# ── NaN guard on feature vector ───────────────────────────────────────────────
@udf(BooleanType())
def has_nan_or_inf(v):
    if v is None:
        return True
    return any(math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x) for x in v.toArray())

train_clean = train_df.filter(~has_nan_or_inf(col("features")))
test_clean  = test_df.filter(~has_nan_or_inf(col("features")))

print("Train rows :", train_clean.count())
print("Test  rows :", test_clean.count())



# ── Train ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
lr = LinearRegression(
    featuresCol="features",
    labelCol=target_col,
    maxIter=100,
    solver="normal",
    regParam=0.0,
    elasticNetParam=0.0,
    standardization=False
)
lr_model = lr.fit(train_clean)

# ── Evaluate ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
predictions = lr_model.transform(test_clean)

evaluator = RegressionEvaluator(labelCol=target_col, predictionCol="prediction")
r2   = evaluator.setMetricName("r2").evaluate(predictions)
rmse = evaluator.setMetricName("rmse").evaluate(predictions)
mae  = evaluator.setMetricName("mae").evaluate(predictions)

print("Intercept :", round(lr_model.intercept, 4))
print("R2        :", round(r2, 4))
print("RMSE      :", round(rmse, 2))
print("MAE       :", round(mae, 2))

# ── SE / t-values / p-values ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
summary = lr_model.summary
coefs   = np.array(lr_model.coefficients.toArray())
n_feats = len(coefs)

try:
    se    = np.array(summary.coefficientStandardErrors[:-1])
    tvals = np.array(summary.tValues[:-1])
    pvals = np.array(summary.pValues[:-1])
    se_method = "exact"
except Exception:
    train_pred = lr_model.transform(train_clean)
    n   = train_pred.count()
    rss_row = train_pred.selectExpr(
        "sum(pow(" + target_col + " - prediction, 2)) as rss"
    ).collect()[0]
    rss = rss_row["rss"]
    mse = rss / (n - n_feats - 1)
    se    = np.full(n_feats, np.sqrt(mse / n))
    tvals = coefs / se
    pvals = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(np.abs(tvals), df=n - n_feats - 1))
    se_method = "approximated"

# ── Feature names from VectorAssembler metadata (ground truth) ────────────────
meta  = train_df.schema["features"].metadata
attrs = meta.get("ml_attr", {}).get("attrs", {})

name_map = {}
for attr_type, attr_list in attrs.items():
    for attr in attr_list:
        name_map[attr["idx"]] = attr["name"]

feature_names = [name_map.get(i, "feature_" + str(i)) for i in range(n_feats)]

n_names = len(feature_names)
if n_names != n_feats:
    raise ValueError("Mismatch: " + str(n_names) + " names vs " + str(n_feats) + " features")

print("Feature names:", feature_names)
# ── Coefficient DataFrame ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ci_lower = coefs - 1.96 * se
ci_upper = coefs + 1.96 * se

coef_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Feature"     : feature_names,
    "Coefficient" : coefs.round(4),
    "Std Error"   : se.round(4),
    "t-value"     : tvals.round(4),
    "p-value"     : pvals.round(4),
    "CI Lower"    : ci_lower.round(4),
    "CI Upper"    : ci_upper.round(4),
    "Significant" : ["Yes" if p < 0.05 else "No" for p in pvals],
})

top15 = coef_df.reindex(
    coef_df["Coefficient"].abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index
).head(15)
print("\nTop 15 features by absolute coefficient:")
print(top15.to_string(index=False))

sig_count = (coef_df["Significant"] == "Yes").sum()
print("\nModel Performance:")
print("  R2   =", round(r2, 4), "-> explains", str(round(r2 * 100, 1)) + "% of variance in salary")
print("  RMSE =", round(rmse, 2), "-> avg prediction error in salary units")
print("  MAE  =", round(mae, 2), "-> median absolute prediction error")
print(str(sig_count) + " of " + str(n_feats) + " features statistically significant (p < 0.05)")
print("SE method:", se_method)
```


###  Polymnomial Regression
from pyspark.ml.regression import LinearRegression
from pyspark.ml.evaluation import RegressionEvaluator
from pyspark.sql.functions import udf, col, isnan
from pyspark.sql.types import BooleanType
from scipy import stats
import numpy as np, pandas as pd, math

@udf(BooleanType())
def has_nan_or_inf(v):
    if v is None: return True
    return any(math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x) for x in v.toArray())

train_clean_poly = train_df.filter(
    col(target_col).isNotNull() & ~isnan(col(target_col))
).filter(~has_nan_or_inf(col("features_poly")))

test_clean_poly = test_df.filter(
    col(target_col).isNotNull() & ~isnan(col(target_col))
).filter(~has_nan_or_inf(col("features_poly")))

lr_poly = LinearRegression(
    featuresCol="features_poly",
    labelCol=target_col,
    maxIter=100,
    solver="normal",
    regParam=0.0,
    elasticNetParam=0.0,
    standardization=False
)
lr_poly_model = lr_poly.fit(train_clean_poly)

predictions_poly = lr_poly_model.transform(test_clean_poly)
evaluator = RegressionEvaluator(labelCol=target_col, predictionCol="prediction")

r2_poly   = evaluator.setMetricName("r2").evaluate(predictions_poly)
rmse_poly = evaluator.setMetricName("rmse").evaluate(predictions_poly)
mae_poly  = evaluator.setMetricName("mae").evaluate(predictions_poly)

summary_poly = lr_poly_model.summary
coefs_poly   = np.array(lr_poly_model.coefficients.toArray())
n_feats_poly = len(coefs_poly)

try:
    se_poly    = np.array(summary_poly.coefficientStandardErrors[:-1])
    tvals_poly = np.array(summary_poly.tValues[:-1])
    pvals_poly = np.array(summary_poly.pValues[:-1])
    se_method_poly = "exact"
except Exception:
    train_pred_poly = lr_poly_model.transform(train_clean_poly)
    n_poly  = train_pred_poly.count()
    rss_poly = train_pred_poly.selectExpr(
        "sum(pow(`" + target_col + "` - prediction, 2)) as rss"
    ).collect()[0]["rss"]
    mse_poly = rss_poly / max(n_poly - n_feats_poly - 1, 1)
    se_poly    = np.full(n_feats_poly, np.sqrt(mse_poly / n_poly))
    tvals_poly = coefs_poly / se_poly
    pvals_poly = 2 * (1 - stats.t.cdf(np.abs(tvals_poly), df=n_poly - n_feats_poly - 1))
    se_method_poly = "approximated"

meta_poly  = train_clean_poly.schema["features_poly"].metadata
attrs_poly = meta_poly.get("ml_attr", {}).get("attrs", {})
name_map_poly = {}
for attr_type, attr_list in attrs_poly.items():
    for attr in attr_list:
        name_map_poly[attr["idx"]] = attr["name"]
feature_names_poly = [name_map_poly.get(i, "feature_" + str(i)) for i in range(n_feats_poly)]

ci_lower_poly = coefs_poly - 1.96 * se_poly
ci_upper_poly = coefs_poly + 1.96 * se_poly

coef_df_poly = pd.DataFrame({
    "Feature"     : feature_names_poly,
    "Coefficient" : coefs_poly.round(4),
    "Std Error"   : se_poly.round(4),
    "t-value"     : tvals_poly.round(4),
    "p-value"     : pvals_poly.round(4),
    "CI Lower"    : ci_lower_poly.round(4),
    "CI Upper"    : ci_upper_poly.round(4),
    "Significant" : ["Yes" if p < 0.05 else "No" for p in pvals_poly],
})

top15_poly = coef_df_poly.reindex(
    coef_df_poly["Coefficient"].abs().sort_values(ascending=False).index
).head(15)
print("Top 15 features by absolute coefficient (Polynomial LR):")
print(top15_poly.to_string(index=False))

sig_poly = (coef_df_poly["Significant"] == "Yes").sum()
print("\nPolynomial LR Performance:")
print("  R2   =", round(r2_poly, 4))
print("  RMSE =", round(rmse_poly, 2))
print("  MAE  =", round(mae_poly, 2))
print(str(sig_poly) + " of " + str(n_feats_poly) + " features significant (p < 0.05)")
print("SE method:", se_method_poly)
```


###  Random Forest Regressor
```{python}
from pyspark.ml.regression import RandomForestRegressor
from pyspark.ml.evaluation import RegressionEvaluator
from pyspark.sql.functions import udf, col, isnan
from pyspark.sql.types import BooleanType
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import math
import os
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

boolean_cols = ["IS_INTERNSHIP", "COMPANY_IS_STAFFING"]

# NaN guard
@udf(BooleanType())
def has_nan_or_inf(v):
    if v is None:
        return True
    return any(math.isnan(x) or math.isinf(x) for x in v.toArray())

train_rf = train_df.filter(
    col(target_col).isNotNull() & ~isnan(col(target_col))
).filter(~has_nan_or_inf(col("features")))

test_rf = test_df.filter(
    col(target_col).isNotNull() & ~isnan(col(target_col))
).filter(~has_nan_or_inf(col("features")))

print("Train rows:", train_rf.count())
print("Test  rows:", test_rf.count())

# Hyperparameter note:
# numTrees and maxDepth are inversely proportional.
# More trees → each can be shallower (less variance per tree, ensemble corrects).
# Fewer trees → each needs more depth to capture complexity.
# numTrees=200, maxDepth=6 is a balanced mid-range choice.
rf = RandomForestRegressor(
    featuresCol="features",
    labelCol=target_col,
    numTrees=200,
    maxDepth=6,
    seed=42
)
rf_model = rf.fit(train_rf)

# Evaluate
predictions = rf_model.transform(test_rf)

evaluator = RegressionEvaluator(labelCol=target_col, predictionCol="prediction")
r2   = evaluator.setMetricName("r2").evaluate(predictions)
rmse = evaluator.setMetricName("rmse").evaluate(predictions)
mae  = evaluator.setMetricName("mae").evaluate(predictions)

print("R2   :", round(r2, 4))
print("RMSE :", round(rmse, 2))
print("MAE  :", round(mae, 2))

# Feature importances
importances = rf_model.featureImportances.toArray()
n_feats     = len(importances)

# Feature names from VectorAssembler metadata
meta  = train_rf.schema["features"].metadata
attrs = meta.get("ml_attr", {}).get("attrs", {})

name_map = {}
for attr_type, attr_list in attrs.items():
    for attr in attr_list:
        name_map[attr["idx"]] = attr["name"]

feature_names = [name_map.get(i, "feature_" + str(i)) for i in range(n_feats)]

importance_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Feature"    : feature_names,
    "Importance" : importances.round(6),
}).sort_values("Importance", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

print("\nTop 10 Feature Importances:")
print(importance_df.head(10).to_string(index=False))

# Seaborn bar plot — top 10
top10 = importance_df.head(10)

os.makedirs("_output", exist_ok=True)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(data=top10, x="Importance", y="Feature", palette="Blues_r", ax=ax)

ax.set_title("Top 10 Feature Importances — Random Forest Regressor",
             fontsize=14, fontweight="bold", pad=12)
ax.set_xlabel("Importance Score", fontsize=11)
ax.set_ylabel("Feature", fontsize=11)
ax.tick_params(labelsize=10)

for i, val in enumerate(top10["Importance"]):
    ax.text(val + 0.0005, i, str(round(val, 4)), va="center", fontsize=9)

sns.despine()
plt.tight_layout()

output_path = "_output/rf_feature_importance.png"
plt.savefig(output_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
print("Saved:", output_path)

print("\nModel Performance:")
print("  R2   =", round(r2, 4), "-> explains", str(round(r2 * 100, 1)) + "% of variance in salary")
print("  RMSE =", round(rmse, 2))
print("  MAE  =", round(mae, 2))
print("  Trees:", 200, "| Max Depth:", 6)
```




###  Compare 3 Models
```{python}
from pyspark.ml.evaluation import RegressionEvaluator
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, rand
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import math
import os

# Use the same test sets each model was trained and evaluated against.
# Do NOT re-filter test_df here — that can produce a different feature vector
# if the FE cell was re-run after the models were fitted.
lr_preds   = lr_model.transform(test_clean)           # features  (from LR cell)
poly_preds = lr_poly_model.transform(test_clean_poly)                                                  # features_poly (from Poly cell)
rf_preds   = rf_model.transform(test_rf)              # features  (from RF cell)

# Metrics
evaluator = RegressionEvaluator(labelCol=target_col, predictionCol="prediction")

rmse_lr   = evaluator.setMetricName("rmse").evaluate(lr_preds)
rmse_poly = evaluator.setMetricName("rmse").evaluate(poly_preds)
rmse_rf   = evaluator.setMetricName("rmse").evaluate(rf_preds)

# AIC  = n·ln(RSS/n) + 2·(k+1)       where k = n_coefficients, +1 for intercept
# BIC  = n·ln(RSS/n) + (k+1)·ln(n)

def compute_aic_bic(model, train_data, label_col):
    n   = train_data.count()
    k   = len(model.coefficients) + 1
    rss = (
        model.transform(train_data)
             .selectExpr(
                 "sum(pow(`" + label_col + "` - prediction, 2)) as rss"
             )
             .collect()[0]["rss"]
    )
    aic = n * math.log(rss / n) + 2 * k
    bic = n * math.log(rss / n) + k * math.log(n)
    return round(aic, 2), round(bic, 2)

# train_clean must be the filtered train set used to fit lr_model (features col)
# train_clean_poly is the filtered train set used to fit lr_poly_model (features_poly col)
aic_lr,   bic_lr   = compute_aic_bic(lr_model,      train_clean,      target_col)
aic_poly, bic_poly = compute_aic_bic(lr_poly_model, train_clean_poly, target_col)
metrics_df = pd.DataFrame({
    "Model" : ["Linear Regression", "Polynomial LR", "Random Forest"],
    "RMSE"  : [round(rmse_lr, 2),   round(rmse_poly, 2),   round(rmse_rf, 2)],
    "AIC"   : [round(aic_lr, 2),    round(aic_poly, 2),    "N/A"],
    "BIC"   : [round(bic_lr, 2),    round(bic_poly, 2),    "N/A"],
})
print(metrics_df.to_string(index=False))

# Collect random sample to pandas for plotting
def sample_to_pandas(spark_df, label_col, n=5000):
    return (
        spark_df
        .select(col(label_col).alias("actual"), col("prediction").alias("predicted"))
        .orderBy(rand(seed=42))
        .limit(n)
        .toPandas()
    )

lr_pdf   = sample_to_pandas(lr_preds,   target_col)
poly_pdf = sample_to_pandas(poly_preds, target_col)
rf_pdf   = sample_to_pandas(rf_preds,   target_col)

# 2x2 Grid Plot
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(14, 12))
fig.suptitle("Actual vs Predicted Salary — Model Comparison",
             fontsize=16, fontweight="bold", y=1.01)

panels = [
    (axes[0, 0], lr_pdf,   "Linear Regression",  rmse_lr,   "#2196F3"),
    (axes[0, 1], poly_pdf, "Polynomial LR",       rmse_poly, "#9C27B0"),
    (axes[1, 0], rf_pdf,   "Random Forest",       rmse_rf,   "#4CAF50"),
]

for ax, pdf, title, rmse, color in panels:
    sns.scatterplot(
        data=pdf, x="actual", y="predicted",
        alpha=0.25, s=12, color=color, ax=ax, linewidth=0
    )
    mn = min(pdf["actual"].min(), pdf["predicted"].min())
    mx = max(pdf["actual"].max(), pdf["predicted"].max())
    ax.plot([mn, mx], [mn, mx], "r--", linewidth=1.5, label="Perfect fit")
    ax.set_title(title + "\nRMSE: " + str(round(rmse, 2)),
                 fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
    ax.set_xlabel("Actual Salary", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_ylabel("Predicted Salary", fontsize=10)
    ax.legend(fontsize=9)
    sns.despine(ax=ax)

# Panel 4: RMSE bar chart
ax4          = axes[1, 1]
model_labels = ["Linear\nRegression", "Polynomial\nLR", "Random\nForest"]
rmse_vals    = [round(rmse_lr, 2), round(rmse_poly, 2), round(rmse_rf, 2)]
bar_colors   = ["#2196F3", "#9C27B0", "#4CAF50"]

bars = ax4.bar(model_labels, rmse_vals, color=bar_colors, edgecolor="white", width=0.5)
for bar, val in zip(bars, rmse_vals):
    ax4.text(
        bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2,
        bar.get_height() + max(rmse_vals) * 0.01,
        str(val), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold"
    )
ax4.set_title("RMSE Comparison", fontsize=12, fontweight="bold")
ax4.set_ylabel("RMSE (lower is better)", fontsize=10)
ax4.set_ylim(0, max(rmse_vals) * 1.2)
sns.despine(ax=ax4)

plt.tight_layout()
os.makedirs("_output", exist_ok=True)
plt.savefig("_output/model_comparison.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
plt.show()
print("Saved: _output/model_comparison.png")
```
